answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can use slashable vouching bonds. A newcomer cannot transact until an established agent locks a bond as its sponsor, a costly signal that puts the sponsor's own standing on the line. The newcomer starts at dawn with zero trust and earns paid work only through peer-attested jobs. If it is caught gaming the system, the bond is slashed and the sponsor loses money and reputation, so to forge a thousand fake identities an attacker must risk a thousand bonds. Honest agents pay nothing extra; attackers pay for every identity they create.
